answer: Agents gain voting weight only after completing randomly assigned tasks whose results are checked against peers, and they must lock a stake that is forfeited if an audit finds deliberate duplication. An attacker cannot merely forge many identities: each must fund a stake and pay for work, while coordinated copies risk losing their deposits. A juniper seed can make task assignment unpredictable, and a prism audit can compare outputs across groups. This raises the cost of a sybil attack without pretending to prove one person per agent.
